findings.rationale: Migration replacements are computed from previously read source, but the commit path never verifies that each target still contains those bytes before renaming over it. A concurrent editor or migration can therefore be silently overwritten.

The materialized filename is derived only from the source stem and PID, then opened through std::fs::write and unconditionally removed on drop. A stale or pre-created file/symlink at that predictable path can be overwritten and subsequently deleted.

Document generation verifies signed approval records against trust keys, but document check exposes no trust-key option and load_approvals_for_check accepts every V2 record without signature verification while copying its key ID and approval metadata into the expected rendering. A forged signed approval and matching document can therefore be reported conformant.

Generation renders AppliedApproval.artifact_digest from target.reviewed_digest, whereas checking renders the same field from target.digest. A legitimately reviewed requirements document whose reviewed bytes differ from the canonical rendering will not round-trip through generate and check with the same approval record.

Approval creation records glossary and evidence digests before rendering, but render_document_for_approval reopens those paths without comparing the loaded digests to the recorded FileInput values. If an input changes between the two reads, the resulting approval can be signed with input hashes that do not describe the bytes used to produce its target digest.
